text:
sree: Noticed a p99 CPU jump on host-side during canary 2.7.4 -> 2.8.0 roll. baseline p99 host cpu ~18%, canary shows ~33% for same qps.

maria: ugh, saw alerts. is it decode or preparse?

sree: traced to tokenization + parse path. flamegraph points to extra memcpy + a small hot loop in slimmux (the new stream chunker). link: https://internal.gfx/flames/5954321987

eli: can you paste the top stack lines?

sree: sure — main diff from prod: kernel auto-switch now considers minibatch shapes; if minibatch < 4 we pick kernel X which has higher per-request prep cost. sample stacks: 
```
parse_slice()
slimmux_emit_chunk()
host_tokenize_buf()
memcpy
kv_cache_lookup_hot()
```

ben: so two things: the kernel selection heuristic + slimmux change could be amplifying KV cache thrash. small batches -> more frequent KV misses -> more work on host.

maria: do we have perf counters showing KV hitrate by batch size?

sree: yes. pulled from canary host: 
```
batch_size  avg_kv_hit  request_count
1-2         0.42        18k
3-4         0.78        7k
5+          0.92        2k
```

eli: wow. that aligns. slim mux fragments requests into micro-chunks when small writev windows occur. more fragments = more separate KV lookups.

ben: hypothesis: kernel X's lower decode-per-token latency only shows up when amortized across larger minibatches; for tiny batches it loses. And slimmux increases fragmentation so effective minibatch size drops.

maria: action plan? rollback slimmux or tweak kernel heuristic?

sree: propose three-step:
1) temporary canary rollback to 2.7.4 slimmux (disable fragmentation) — quick mitigation.
2) metrics: add KV hit-rate by "fragment_count" tag + p99 host cpu by kernel variant.
3) longer term: change kernel selection to prefer kernel Y for effective minibatch < 4 or when fragmentation > 2. Also add prefetch to kv_lookup to reduce memcpy hotpath.

eli: +1. also add a tiny coalescer in host preparse to combine fragments from same connection within 2ms window. cheap and should lift effective batch size.

ben: can we test locally? i can run loadgen with scripted fragmentation.

sree: that would be great. test permutations: kernel X vs Y, slimmux on/off, prefetch on/off. target bench: 5k reqs/s with 200ms model latency to stress host.

maria: I'll open a quick dashboard panel for kv_hit_by_frag and host_cpu_by_kernel.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2.8.0 started at 2026-03-21T12:14:00Z -> 20% (hosts: host-a3, host-b7)

eli: small note: I instrumented a microtrace that shows the memcpy originates from converting iovec->continuous buffer for the tokenizer. we can avoid by passing iovec into tokenizer in-place. low risk change.

sree: nice. that + kv prefetch might shave ~6-8% host CPU on small batches.

ben: i'll start a local harness run now and post numbers in this thread.

maria: ping me once you have numbers, i'll throttle canary if needed. :thumbsup:

elapsed: 00:00:00

ben: (later) quick results: with scripted fragmentation (avg frag count 3.4)
- kernel X + slimmux on: p99 host cpu 34%
- kernel Y + slimmux on: p99 host cpu 27%
- kernel X + slimmux off: p99 host cpu 22%
- kernel Y + slimmux off + prefetch: p99 host cpu 16%

sree: that confirms. i'll propose immediate rollback of slimmux fragment on canary and follow up with kernel selection tweak + prefetch patch.

maria: rolling back slimmux on canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy rollback to 2.7.4 initiated at 2026-03-21T12:37:00Z -> 20%

eli: opened PR for tokenizer iovec patch: https://phabricator/r/PR12345 (small unsafe cast, perf test included)

sree: opened ticket INF-981: "kernel-selection: prefer kernel Y for effective_minibatch <4 and add kv prefetch"

maria: thanks team. we'll monitor KV hit rates and p99 for next 2 hours.

ben: TL;DR: root cause = fragmenting stream + kernel heuristic mismatch -> KV thrash + memcpy hotpath. mitigation = rollback slimmux fragments + kernel heuristic + tokenizer iovec + kv prefetch.

sree: adding note to postmortem after stabilization.

maria: closing loop when metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
